THE HOLY SPIRIT

1. For the Holy Spirit

Almighty God, you have given us the commandment to pray for the gift of the Holy Spirit. We pray through Jesus Christ our advocate that you would send us your Holy Spirit, that he may quicken our hearts by your saving Word and lead us into all truth, that he may guide, instruct, enlighten, govern, comfort and sanctify us for eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.  (TLH 3)

2. For the Holy Spirit

Almighty God, send your Holy Spirit into our hearts, that he may govern and guide us according to your will, comfort us in all our temptations and afflictions, defend us from all error, and lead us into all truth, that we may be steadfast in the faith, increase in love and in all good works, and in the end, obtain eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Brunswick-Luneburg 1564, Pentecost, TLH 4, SBH 91)

3. For the Holy Spirit

O Lord God, heavenly Father, let your Holy Spirit dwell in us, that he may enlighten and lead us into all truth, and always defend us from all trouble; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 7)

4. For the Holy Spirit

O Lord God, heavenly Father, by the blessed light of your divine Word you have led us to the knowledge of your Son. Refresh us with the grace of your Holy Spirit, that we may always walk in the light of your truth, rejoice with sure confidence in Christ our Savior, and finally be brought to eternal salvation; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 64)

5. For the Holy Spirit

Almighty and eternal God, in your great mercy in Jesus Christ your Son you give us forgiveness of sin and all things pertaining to life and godliness. Send your Holy Spirit, that he may rule our hearts, so that we may always be mindful of your fatherly mercy, strive to mortify the flesh and overcome the world, serve you in holiness and pureness of living, and give you constant thanks for all your goodness; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Brandenburg-Calenberg, 1569, TLH 65, SBH 90)

SPECIAL GIFTS

6. For Spiritual Renewal

O Lord God, heavenly Father, you gave your only Son to die for our sins and rise again for our justification. Renew us by your Holy Spirit that through the power of Christ’s resurrection we may dwell with him forever, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen. (Loehe, Agende 1853, Easter, first part from Austria 1571, also in Book of Common Prayer 1662, TLH 8, SBH 88)

7. For Spiritual Renewal

Almighty God, you gave us your only Son to take our nature on himself. Since we have been born again and have been made your children by adoption and grace, renew us daily by your Holy Spirit; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, Christmas, based on Gelasian, TLH 51, SBH 89)

8. For Spiritual Illumination

Almighty God, let the brightness of your glory shine on us, and let the Light from Light by your Holy Spirit shine in the hearts of all who have been born again by your grace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 61)

9. For Guidance into Truth

O God, enlighten our minds by the Spirit who proceeds from you, that, as your Son has promised, we may be led into all truth; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Vespers within the Octave of Pentecost, TLH 50, SBH 92)

10. For Grace to Receive the Word

Blessed Lord, you have caused all Holy Scriptures to be written for our learning. Grant that we may hear them, read, mark, learn, and inwardly digest them, that being given patience and comfort by your holy Word, we may embrace and ever hold fast the blessed hope of eternal life, which you have given us in our Savior Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer, 1549, Advent 2, TLH 49, SBH 93)

11. For Faith

Almighty and eternal God, you have given many great and precious promises to those who believe. Help us to believe in your Son Jesus Christ, firmly and without doubt, that our faith in your sight may never be reproved. hear us, O Lord, through our Savior Jesus Christ. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, St. Thomas’ Day, TLH 58, SBH 103)

12. For Constancy

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, in your tender love towards us sinners, you have given us your Son, that believing on him we might have eternal life. Send your Holy Spirit, that we may continue steadfast in this faith to the end, and may come to eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 5)

13. For Faith, Hope and Love

Almighty God, grant us a steadfast faith in Jesus Christ, a cheerful hope in your mercy and a sincere love for you and for one another; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Döbers Mass, Nuremberg 1525, TLH 1, SBH 97)

14. For Love to God

O God, you make all things to work together for the good of those who love you. Pour such steadfast love toward you into our hearts that the pure desires your Spirit has stirred in us may not be turned aside by any temptation; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 68)

15. For Love to God

O God, through the grace of your Holy Spirit you pour the gifts of love into the hearts of your faithful people. Give us health of mind and body, that we may love you with all our strength, and with all our hearts do what is pleasing to you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gregorian, TLH 56, SBH 98)

16. For Charity

O Lord, you have taught us all our deeds without love are worth nothing. Send your Holy Spirit and pour into our hearts that most excellent gift of love, the true bond of peace and of all virtues, that we may always live in love before you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 69, SBH 100)

17. For Grace to do God's Will

Almighty God, give us grace that we may cast aside the works of darkness, and put on us the armor of light, now in the time of this mortal life, just as your Son Jesus Christ came to visit us in great humility; that in the last day when he will come again in his glorious majesty to judge both the quick and the dead, we may rise to the life immortal; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, Advent 1, TLH 55, SBH 101)

18. For Grace to use our Gifts

O Lord God Almighty, you give your servants many kinds of gifts from the Holy Spirit. Do not leave us destitute of your many gifts, but give us grace to use them always to your honor and glory; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, St. Barnabas’ Day, TLH 48, SBH 106)

19. For Divine Guidance and help

O Lord, with your love direct us in all our doings, and always help us, that in all our works begun, continued, and ended in you, we may glorify your holy name; and finally, by your mercy obtain eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gregorian, Ember Saturday in Lent, Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 59, SBH 113)

20. For Divine Guidance and help

O almighty and eternal God, direct, sanctify and govern our hearts and bodies in the ways of your laws, and in the works of your commandments; that, through your mighty protection, now and always, we may be preserved in body and soul; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Sarum Breviary, Prime, Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 60, SBH 105)

21. For Divine Guidance and help

Almighty and eternal God, you enable us both to want and to do what is good and acceptable to your divine majesty. Let your fatherly hand always be over us. Let your Holy Spirit always be with us, and lead us in the knowledge and obedience of your Word, that in the end we may obtain eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Hermann’s Ref. of Cologne, 1543, Confirmation, Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 9, SBH 94)

22. For Aid against Temptation

O God, you justify the ungodly, and you do not desire the death of the sinner. Graciously help and shield your servants who trust in your mercy, that no temptations may separate us from you, and that we may serve you without ceasing; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 57)

23. For Aid in Temptation

Almighty and eternal God, by your Son you promised us forgiveness of sins and eternal life. Rule and govern our hearts by your Holy Spirit, that in our daily need and especially in all times of temptation we may seek help from him, and obtain it by a true and living faith in your Word; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Saxony, Duke Henry, 1539, TLH 6, SBH 12)

24. For Repentance

Merciful Father, give us grace that we may never presume to sin. But if at any time we offend you, lead us to truly repent of our offences, and in living faith obtain forgiveness of all our sins; solely through the merits of your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer, Mary Magdalene’s Day, TLH 52, SBH 13)

25. For Pardon

O Lord, hear the prayers of your people, and spare those who confess their sins to you, that you may bestow on us both pardon and peace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 53)

26. For Deliverance from Sin

O Lord, show us your unspeakable mercy, that you may set us free from our sins and rescue us from the punishments which we deserve for our sins; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 54)

27. For Grace to know and follow Christ

O almighty God, to know you is eternal life. Teach us to know your Son Jesus Christ as the Way, the Truth, and the Life; that following him we may steadfastly walk in the way that leads to eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 63)

28. For Grace to follow Christ

Almighty God, you have given your only Son, to be a sacrifice for our sins and an example of godly life. Give us grace that we may always most thankfully receive this priceless gift from him, and daily strive to follow the blessed steps of his most holy life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, Easter 2, TLH 62, SBH 107)

29. For Patience

O God, by the meek endurance of your only Son you beat down the pride of the old enemy. Help us rightly to treasure in our hearts what our Lord has borne for our sakes, that following his example we may bear all our troubles with patience; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Missale Romanum, Church Book 1878, TLH 71, SBH 108)

30. For Contentment

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, you feed the birds and clothe the flowers, and you care for us as a father for his children. Guard our hearts against faithlessness and anxiety. By your Holy Spirit, help us to live to the hallowing of your name, the coming of your kingdom, and the doing of your will, so that we may cast all our cares on you and in unwavering faith, trust in you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Austria 1571, SBH 110)

31. For Steadfastness in Affliction

Almighty and most merciful God, we must endure sufferings and death with our Lord Jesus Christ, before we enter with him into eternal glory. Grant us grace that we may always subject ourselves to your holy will, and continue steadfast in the true faith to the end of our lives, and always find peace and joy in the blessed hope of the resurrection of the dead, and of the glory of the world to come; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Saxe-Coburg 1626, Burial, TLH 34, SBH 111)

32. For Humility

O God, you resist the proud and give grace to the humble. Give us true humility, like the humility your only Son revealed in himself, that we may never exalt ourselves and provoke your wrath, but in all lowliness, partake of the gifts of your grace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 70)

33. For Purity

Almighty God, to whom all hearts are open, all desires known, and from whom no secrets are hidden, cleanse the thoughts of our hearts by the inspiration of your Holy Spirit, that we may perfectly love you, and worthily magnify your holy name; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Late Gregorian, Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 66, SBH 112)

34. For Holiness

O God, your strength is made perfect in weakness. Mortify all vices in us and strengthen us by your grace, that by the innocence of our lives and the steadfastness of our faith even to death, we may glorify your holy name; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 67)

35. for a Blessed Death

Almighty God, confirm your unworthy servants in your grace, that in the hour of our death the adversary may not prevail against us, but that we may be found worthy of eternal life through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 72)

36. For the Blessedness of heaven

Almighty and eternal God, you gave your only Son to be a High Priest of good things to come. Grant that we, your unworthy servants, may have our share in the company of the blessed; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Church Book 1878, TLH 73, SBH 118)

37. For Peace

O God, you are the author of peace and lover of concord. In knowing you we have eternal life, and serving you is perfect freedom. Defend us, your humble servants, against all assaults of our enemies. that trusting in your defense, we may not fear the power of any adversaries; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Brandenburg-Nuremburg 1533, Book of Common Prayer 1549, TLH 74, SBH 119)

THE CHURCH

38. For the Church

Almighty God, give to your Church your Holy Spirit and the wisdom which comes down from above, that your Word may not be bound, but have free course and be preached to the joy and edifying of Christ's holy people, that we may serve you in steadfast faith, and confess your name as long as we live; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Brandenburg-Nuremberg 1522, Church Book 1868, TLH 10, SBH 2).

39. For the Church

Merciful Lord, cast the bright beams of your light on your Church, that it may be instructed by the doctrine of the blessed apostles, and walk in the light of your truth, and at last attain the light of eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 11)

40. For the Church

O Lord, in your favor receive the prayers of your church. Deliver it from all trouble and error that it may serve you in safety and freedom, and grant us your peace in our time; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Leonine, Gelasian, TLH 13, SBH 3)

41. For the Protection and Peace of the Church

Almighty and eternal God, you want all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. We pray through Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior, impart the grace and help of your Holy Spirit to all ministers of your Word, that they may purely teach it to the saving of people; by your Almighty power and unsearchable wisdom, bring to nothing all the counsels of those who hate your Word, and who would destroy it by corrupt teaching or with violent hands, and enlighten them with the knowledge of your glory; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life, in a pure faith learn the riches of your heavenly grace, and in holiness and righteousness serve you, the only true God; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 18)

42. For those who have erred

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, you always have mercy. In your fatherly love, correct those who have erred and gone astray from the truth of your holy Word, and to bring them to know their error, that they may again with sincere faith receive and hold fast your unchangeable truth; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 19)

43. For those who have erred

O almighty, merciful, and gracious God and Father, with our whole heart we pray for all who have forsaken the Christian faith, all who have wandered from any part of it, or are in doubt or temptation because of the corruptors of your Word. Visit them as a Father, reveal to them their error, and bring them back from their wanderings; that they may wholeheartedly take pleasure in the pure truth of your Word alone and be made wise for eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 20)

44. For the Unity in the Faith

O Christ, bring to nothing the divisions of heresy which seek to subvert your truth. Since you are acknowledged in heaven and in earth as one and Lord, may your people gathered from all nations, and serve you in unity of faith; for you live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen. (TLH 22)

45. For the Unity in the Faith

O God, you restore to the right way those who have gone astray. You gather those who are scattered and preserve those who are gathered. In your tender mercy, pour on your Christian people the grace of unity, that all divisions will be healed, and your flock will be united to the true Shepherd of your Church, and will worthily serve you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 21)

46. For the Children of the Church

Almighty and eternal God, you are not willing that not one of these little ones should perish, and you sent your only Son to seek and to save those who were lost, and through him you said, “Let the little children to come to me, and forbid them not, for of such is the kingdom of God.” Bless and govern the children of your Church by your Holy Spirit, that they may grow in grace and in the knowledge of your Word. Protect and defend them against all danger and harm, giving your holy angels charge over them; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Saxe-Coburg 1626. Tr. Paul Zeller Strodach, Common Service Book. TLH 14, SBH 17)

47. For the Children of the Parish

Blessed Lord Jesus, you have taught us that we must become like little children to come to your kingdom, and you loved and blessed them most tenderly. Grant that our children may be drawn to you by your good Spirit and always be kept in your service, so that walking in your way they may declare your praise and be one with us in the confession of your holy name; who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen.

48. For Catechumens

Almighty and eternal God, you always cause your Church to grow, and with your light and grace you strengthen the hearts of those you have given new birth through water and the Spirit. Grant that our catechumens increase both in faith and knowledge, that they may rejoice in their baptism and grow as members of the holy body of your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Good Friday, SBH 16)

THE MINISTRY

49. For the Ministry

Almighty and Gracious God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, you have commanded us to pray that you would send forth laborers into your harvest. In your mercy give us true teachers and ministers of your Word, and put your saving Gospel in their hearts and on their lips, that they may truly fulfill your command, and preach nothing contrary to your holy Word; that we may be warned, instructed, nurtured, comforted and strengthened by your heavenly Word, and do those things which are well-pleasing to you, and profitable to us; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 16)

50. For the Ministry

O Almighty God, by your Son Jesus Christ, you gave your holy apostles many excellent gifts, and commanded them to feed your flock. Make all pastors preach your holy Word diligently, and the people to follow obediently that they may receive the crown of eternal glory; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 17)

51. For the Ministry

Almighty and eternal God, you alone do great wonders. Send down on your ministers and on the congregations committed to their care the Spirit of your grace. Pour on them the continual dew of your blessing that they may truly please you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Cranmer: Litany, TLH 15, SBH 19)

MISSIONS

52. For Missions

O God, our Protector, look on the face of Jesus, your Anointed One, who gave himself for the redemption of all, and grant that from the rising of the sun until its setting, your name may be great among all nations, and that in every place, sacrifice and a pure offering may be made to your name; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Missale Romanum, Mass for the Propogation of the Faith, TLH 12, SBH 23)

53. For Missions

Almighty God, heavenly Father, through your Son, Jesus Christ, you gave the command to your people to go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. Give us a ready will to obey your Word. As we support the labors of others, help us to serve you, that others may support us in our labors; and that we with them, and they with us, may attain to eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

54. For Missions

O God, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life: Look with compassion on the heathen who do not know you, and on the many who are scattered like sheep without a shepherd. Give us your grace that all your believers may be the messengers of your Gospel, seek those who are lost, and restore them to you. And when you have gathered your people, strengthen, nurture, protect and guide them by the true Shepherd and Bishop of souls, Jesus Christ, your Son, to whom, with you and the Holy Spirit be honor and power, dominion and glory, now and forever. Amen. (Henry Eyster Jacobs, 1917, Common Service Book, SBH 26)

55. For the Commissioning of Missionaries

Almighty God, you make all things in heaven and earth serve your gracious will. We commit to your care and protection these your servants whom we send forth in your name. Fulfill the promise made through your Son to be with them always, whatever be the perils they may meet, or the trials they may undergo. Bless them with your continual favor, give them many souls as the reward of their labor, and in every hour of conflict, uncertainty and doubt strengthen and uphold them, and give them your peace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

56 For the Heathen

Almighty and eternal God, you do not desire the death of a sinner but want all people to repent and live. Hear our prayers for the heathen. Take away sin from their hearts and turn them from their idols to the living and true God and to your only Son, and gather them into your holy Church to the glory of your name; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.  (TLH 24)

57 For the Jews

Almighty and eternal God, you love to show mercy. Hear the prayers which we offer for your ancient people, that, acknowledging Jesus Christ as the Light of truth they may be delivered from their darkness; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 23)

58. For the Hallowing of the Lord's Day

O Lord God, heavenly Father, rule and guide us by your Holy Spirit that we hear and receive your holy Word with our whole heart and hallow your Holy Day, in order that we also may be sanctified, learn to place all our trust and hope in Jesus Christ your Son, and following him, be led safely through all evil, until through your grace, we come to eternal life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

59. Morning

Grant us, O Lord, to live this day in gladness and peace, without stumbling and without stain, that reaching the evening victorious over all temptation, we may praise you, the eternal God,

for you govern all things, and are praised now and forever. Amen. (Mozarabic Breviary, Lauds, Advent 1, Bright, Ancient Collects, p. 8, SBH 80).

60. Morning

O Lord, King of heaven and earth, order, hallow, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, and our thoughts, words and actions according to your commandments; through your Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen (Breviarum Romanum, Prime, SBH 81)

61. Evening

Lighten our darkness, Lord, we pray; and in your mercy, defend us from all perils and dangers of this night; for the love of your only Son, our Savior Jesus Christ. Amen. (Geleasian, Book of Common Prayer 1549, Sarum Breviary, TLH 47, SBH 86)

INTERCESSIONS

62. For Those in Affliction

Almighty and eternal God, you are the comfort of the sorrowful and the strength of the weak. Graciously hear the prayers of those who call out to you in any trouble or distress, that in all their needs they may receive your abundant help and know your immeasurable comfort; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Good Friday, TLH 33, SBH 35)

63. For those in Affliction

Almighty God, do not cast away your people who cry to you in their tribulation; but for the glory of your name be pleased to help all who are afflicted; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 35)

64. For those in Affliction

O Lord, look down from heaven, see, visit and relieve your servants, for whom we offer our prayers. Look on them with the eyes of your mercy. Give them comfort and sure confidence in you. Defend them from the danger of the enemy, and keep them in perpetual peace and safety; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Sarum, Book of Common Prayer 1549, SBH 36)

65. For the Sick

Almighty and eternal God, the eternal salvation of those who believe, hear our prayers for your servants who are sick, for whom we ask the aid of your mercy, that being restored to health, they may render thanks to you in your Church; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Gelasian, Church Book 1878, SBH 37)

66. For Mothers

Almighty and eternal God and Father, Creator of all things, your Son, our Lord was born of a human mother, and he alone makes our labors easy and our burdens light. Gracious Father, Lord and God, preserve and guard all mothers and keep them in your care. Do not forsake them in their troubles, but deliver them for their joy and for the glory of your goodness; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 38)

67. For those who are innocently imprisoned

Almighty God, you brought the apostle Peter out of prison. Have mercy on all who are innocently imprisoned and set them free from their bonds, that we may rejoice in their deliverance, and continually give praise to you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 31)

68. For our Enemies

Almighty and eternal God, through your only Son, our blessed Lord, you commanded us to love our enemies, to do good to those who hate us, and to pray for those who persecute us. Move and lead our enemies to true repentance, that they may love and of one mind and heart with us and with your whole Church; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 27)

69. In Time of Great Sickness

Almighty and most merciful God, our heavenly Father: We, your erring children, humbly confess to you, that we have justly deserved the discipline you have sent on us for our sins; but in your boundless goodness move us to true repentance, graciously forgive our sins, remove from us or lighten the punishment we deserve and strengthen us by your grace, that as obedient children we may be subject to your will, and bear our afflictions in patience; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 39)

70. In Time of Drought

O God, most Merciful Father, look on our needs and send a fruitful rain on us to revive the earth and to refresh its fruits, that we may praise and glorify your name for your mercy; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 40)

71. In Time of Unseasonable Weather

O Lord God, heavenly Father, you are gracious and merciful, and you have promised that you will hear us when we call on you in our troubles. Do not look on our sins and evil deeds, but on our needs, and in your mercy, send us such favorable weather, that the earth may yield its crops at the proper time, and by your goodness we will receive our daily bread, learn to know you as a merciful God, and always give thanks to you for your goodness; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 41)

THE NATION

72. For Our Country

Almighty God, you have given us a land where we are free to read and hear your Word, confess your name and work together for the extension of your kingdom. May the liberty given us be continued to our children and our children’s children, that the power of the gospel may here increase to the blessing of all the nations of the earth and to your eternal glory; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Henry Eyster Jacobs, 1917, Common Service Book, SBH 47)

73. For Our Nation

O God, you led our ancestors to this land where they found refuge from oppression and freedom to worship you. Always guide our nation in the way of your truth and peace, so that we enjoy the blessing you have promised to the people whose God is the Lord; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Paul Zeller Strodach, 1917, Common Service Book, SBH 46)

74. For Those in Authority

O merciful Father in heaven, all rule and authority in the kingdoms of the world comes from you and you hold in your hand all the might of humanity. You have instituted the governing authorities that exist for the punishment of those who do wrong and for the approval of those who do good. Look on your servants, the President of the United States, the governor of this state, our judges and officials, and all the rulers of the earth. May all who have authority work as your servants and use their authority according to your will and command. Enlighten and defend them by your name, O God. Give them wisdom and understanding, that under their peaceful governing your people may be guarded and directed in righteousness, quietness and unity. God of our salvation, protect and prolong their lives, that we, with them, may declare the praise of your name; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 25)

75. In Time of National Distress

O Lord God, heavenly Father, by our evil doings and constant disobedience we have deserved your punishment, but for your name's sake spare us. Restrain the harmful power of the enemy, and protect your suffering people, that your Word may be declared faithfully and without hindrance, and that we, amending our sinful lives, may walk obediently to your holy commandments; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 28)

76. In Time of National Distress

O Lord, look mercifully on the affliction of your people. Do not let our sins destroy us, but let your almighty mercy save us; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 29)

77. In Time of National Distress

Most loving and gracious Lord God, you discipline us for our sins like a loving father who wants to correct his children. We flee to your tender and fatherly compassion alone, praying that, as a father pities his children, you would pity us miserable sinners; turn away your righteous wrath and not give us over to deserved death, but deliver us, that we may now and always praise you, O gracious God and Father, who does not desire the death of sinners, but rather that they may turn from their wickedness and live; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 30)

78. National Thanksgiving

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, your mercies are new to us every morning, and though we have not deserved your goodness, you abundantly provide for all the needs of our bodies and souls. Give us your Holy Spirit that we may heartily acknowledge your merciful goodness toward us, give thanks for all your benefits, and serve you in willing obedience; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 43)

79. National Thanksgiving

Almighty and most merciful God, in your fatherly wisdom you chasten us for our sins, so that we might not continue in impenitence and false confidence and perish with the ungodly. We give you thanks and praise that in your wrath you have remembered mercy, turning away from us your just anger, and have graciously delivered us out of our affliction; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 44)

THANKSGIVING

80. For the Blessings of Redemption

O Lord God, heavenly Father, we give you thanks, that of your great goodness and mercy, you sent your only Son to become fully human, and to redeem us from sin and eternal death. Enlighten our hearts by your Holy Spirit, that we may always give you sincere thanks for your grace, and be comforted with it in all times of trouble and temptation; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 2)

81. General

O Lord God, heavenly Father, because of your goodness we receive many abundant gifts from you, and you daily guard us against all evil. Give us your Holy Spirit, that we may acknowledge your goodness with all our heart, and may now and always thank and praise your loving kindness and tender mercy; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 42)

FOR ANSWER TO PRAYER

82. For Answer to Prayer

Almighty God, you are pleased to hear the prayers we bring you, and you promise that when two or three are gathered in your name, you will grant their requests. O Lord, fulfill the desires and petitions of your servants, as you know is best for them, giving us knowledge of your truth here, and in the world to come life eternal; for you live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen. (Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, Cranmer: Litany 1544, TLH 75, SBH 121)

83. For Answer to Prayer

Almighty God, fountain of all wisdom, you know our needs before we ask, and our ignorance in asking. Have compassion on us in our weakness, and give us all those things we dare not ask because of our unworthiness, and the things we cannot ask because of our blindness; for the worthiness of your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, Post Communion, TLH 76, SBH 122)

84. For Answer to Prayer

Almighty God, you have promised to hear the prayers of those who pray in your Son's name. Hear our prayers and supplications to you, and give us what we have asked for according to your will, to the relief of our needs, and to praise of your glory; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1549, Post Communion, TLH 77, SBH 123)

Additional Collects

85. For the Nation

O God, in this land you have made the people the servants of your just rule. Turn their hearts to you, that holding their citizenship as a trust from you, they may guard, defend and use it according to your will, and that, serving you with willing, joyful and obedient hearts, they may cherish their freedom as a blessing of your Gospel, and strive to bring it to all peoples; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Henry Eyster Jacobs, 1917, Common Service Book, SBH 45)

86. For the President, and Those in Authority

Almighty and Eternal God, look on the President of the United States, his advisors, and all others in authority over us. Guide them by your Holy Spirit, that they may be high in purpose, wise in counsel, unwavering in duty, and in the administration of their solemn charge may wholly serve your will, uphold the honor of our nation, secure the protection of our people, and bring victory to our righteous cause; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Paul Zeller Strodach, Common Service Book, 1919, SBH 48)

87. For the Church in Time of War

O Lord, God of our Fathers, your merciful ear is open to our prayer, and from you alone comes our help. In compassion remember your people, on whom has fallen the scourge of war, that they may take to heart your righteous judgments, be prepared for all trials, sustained and comforted in all distresses, and be graciously delivered, in your own time and way, from all threatening calamities; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

88. For the Church in Time of War

O Lord Jesus Christ, you established your Church on earth, and commanded your disciples to be your witnesses among all nations. Grant to your faithful people boldness to confess your name in all the labors and distresses of this time. Enable them by your Holy Spirit to be among their fellowmen as those who serve, turning the hearts of others to you, uplifting the weak, comforting the sorrowing, and speaking peace to the poor and afflicted; you live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen.

89. For the Church in Time of War

O Lord Jesus Christ, you have promised to be with us always, even to the end of the world. Look upon the trials and sorrows of your suffering members, wherever they may be. Sanctify their afflictions by your loving presence, strengthen them to endure hardship, and enable them to carry their cross after you and be faithful to death, that, at the last they may come to the glory you will reveal, where you live and reign with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen.

90. For the Army

O God, you are the shield and armor for all who trust in you. Stretch forth your mighty hand over the Army of the United States and those who serve in it, that strengthened with your might, they may be enabled to overcome every danger that threatens, and be to our land a sure defense against all our foes; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

91. For the Navy

O Lord Jesus Christ, at your word of peace the waves of the sea were still. Preserve the navy of the United States and those who serve from the perils of great waters and the snares and violence of our enemies, that they may guard our land against all those who would destroy or restrain its liberties, so that all the inhabitants may have peace and freedom to serve you; who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen.

92. For Those in Our Country's Service in Time of War

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, protect all those who are in the service of our country, guarding them from all harm and danger of body and soul. Sustain and comfort those at home, especially in their hours of loneliness, anxiety, and sorrow. Prepare the dying for death and the living for your service. Give success to our arms on land and sea and in the air, and grant to us and all nations a speedy, just and lasting peace, to the glory of your Name and the coming of your Kingdom; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Henry Eyster Jacobs, Common Service Book 1917, SBH 49)

93. For Chaplains

O Gracious Father, richly bless on the chaplains who serve the men in the armed forces, and all who minister to the souls of those who go forth to war. Help them by your Holy Spirit to wage war against sin, and to lead men to Christ as the only Savior. Give them grace and strength to follow his example in their life and conversation, and so bless their ministry that they may awaken the careless, strengthen the weak, confirm and encourage the doubting and despairing, comfort the suffering and speak peace to the dying; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

94. For the Ministry of Mercy

O most merciful Father, you commit our fellowmen and their needs to our love and care. Graciously be with and prosper all those who seek and serve the sick and wounded. Let their work be abundantly blessed in bringing ease to the suffering, comfort to the sorrowing, and peace to the dying, knowing that whatever they do for the least of these, Christ's brothers and sisters, they do it to him, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. Amen. (Paul Zeller Strodach, Common Service Book 1917, SBH 52)

95. For the Sick, Wounded and Captives

Almighty and eternal God, you are the comfort of the sorrowful, and the strength of the weak. Hear the prayers of those who cry to you in tribulation and distress, especially the prayers of those who are sick or wounded, in peril of death, or held captive in the power of the enemy; so that in all their needs they may know and receive your help and comfort; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

96. For the Bereaved

Have compassion, O Lord, on all who mourn and on all who are lonely and deserted. Be their Comforter and Friend. Give them earthly comfort as you know to be best for them, and, bringing them to fuller knowledge of your love, wipe away all their tears; for the sake of Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen. (Luther Dotterer Reed, 1917, Common Service Book, SBH 54)

97. For Victory

O God, our refuge and strength, our ever-present help in trouble, protect and prosper our beloved country in this time of war. Make us a people worthy to be entrusted with victory, and use, direct and bless our armed forces that they may be your chosen instruments in overcoming wrong and establishing liberty, truth and righteousness in the earth; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

98. For Peace

Eternal Father, by sending your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, you pronounced your peace to the world, and in the blood of his cross you opened the way to peace with you for all humanity. Turn all people to the cross, and kindle every heart with your Holy Spirit that all may accept Christ as the way of life, that by following his holy example and burning with his zeal to serve, all people may become one family in him, and your peace possess every heart and rule in all the nations of the world; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

99. For the Discomfiture of the Enemies of the Nation

O Lord God Almighty, you alone cast down tyrants and still the noise and tumult of the people. Frustrate the plans of those who secretly devise trouble, and bring the dealings of the violent to nothing. Remove the unjust from high places and stop the lawless from causing trouble. Put down all envious and malicious passions and subdue the haters and evil-doers, that the whole world may have rest before you and that all nations may serve you; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (Book of Common Prayer 1661, SBH 55)

100. For the Maintenance of the Gospel

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, you give us our daily bread in answer to our prayers. Do not withhold from us, or from our children's children, or from our land, or from the people of any nation of the earth, your holy Word, the Bread of Life, but grant that the seed of your living Word may be sown everywhere, and that its fruits may abound to eternal life by your grace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen (Henry Eyster Jacobs, Common Service Book, SBH 27)

101. For the Parents and Friends of Men in the Service

Our Father in heaven, you are always the comfort and help of your people. Be near all who are lonely and sad because of the absence of loved ones in the service of our country. Be their strength and stay in this difficult time of trial, and help them to cast all their burdens on you. Comfort all who suffer loss, giving to them the spirit of submission and an abiding faith in you and in your Word, and fill their hearts with your peace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

APPENDIX:

PRAYERS IN The Lutheran Hymnal THAT WERE NOT IN Common Service Book

O Lord, forgive our enemies and those who maliciously use us. Change their hearts that they may walk with us in humility and peace; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. (TLH 26)

O Lord, hear the prayers of your church. Deliver us from all adversities that we may serve you with a quiet mind and enjoy your peace all the days of our life; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. (TLH 32)

Glory to you, O God most holy! Glory to you, O God most high! Glory to you, O King of heaven and earth! You sustain us with your fatherly kindness. Fill us with joy and gladness in the Holy Spirit, that we may be blameless in your sight through Jesus Christ our Lord on the day when you reward each according to his deeds; through him who has redeemed us from the shame and curse of sin, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH 45, from a prayer by Wilhelm Loehe in Seed Grains of Prayer, #26)

Lord God, almighty Father, eternal God, you have brought us to the beginning of this day. Defend us today with your saving power so that we neither fall into sin nor run into any danger, but in everything we do, subject our words and direct our thoughts to what is right in your sight; through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, now and forever. (TLH 46, also in Matins)

Morning Prayer

In the name of God, the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Amen.

I thank you, my heavenly Father, through Jesus Christ, your dear Son, that you have kept me this night from all harm and danger. And I pray that you would keep me this day also from sin and every evil, that all my doings and life may please you. For into your hands I commend myself, my body, my soul and all things. Let your holy angel be with me, that the evil foe may have no power over me. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#1)

O crucified Lord Jesus Christ, as the patient Lamb of God you suffered the most shameful death on the cross and redeemed me with your precious blood from all sins, from death and from the power of the devil. Assure me of this redemption through your Word. Govern my heart with your Holy Spirit. Preserve me with your divine love, and hide me, both soul and body, in your holy wounds. Wash me clean from all my sins. Teach me to live a life of good works, and finally lead me from this world of sorrows to your eternal joy and glory. Jesus Christ, my faithful Savior, you are my only comfort, hope and life. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#2)

Evening prayer

In the name of God, the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Amen.

I thank you, my heavenly Father, through Jesus Christ, your dear Son, that you have graciously kept me this day. And I pray that you would forgive me all my sins where I have done wrong, and graciously keep me this night. For into your hands I commend myself, my body, my soul and all things. Let your holy angel be with me, that the evil foe may have no power over me. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#3)

O Lord Jesus Christ, patient Lamb of God, you are the holy sacrificial offering for all my sins, and not for mine only, but for the sins of the whole world. I most heartily thank you for keeping my body and soul under your protecting care this day. Graciously pardon and forgive all the sins I have committed this day, both through the weakness of my old evil nature and the temptations of the devil, all of which sorely oppress my heart and conscience. Cover me this night with the wings of your grace and grant that my body may sleep in safety while my soul watches for your glorious coming to judgment, ready to enter your blessed kingdom of glory. Grant this, O Lord, for the sake of your suffering and death. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#4)

Before meals

The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food in due season. You open your hand; you satisfy the desire of every living thing. (Psalm 145:15-16) (TLH, p. 118#5)

Bless us, O Lord, and these your gifts which we receive through your bountiful goodness, through Christ, Our Lord. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#6)

After meals

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever. He gives food to all flesh (Psalm 136:1, 25). He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens that cry. His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man, but the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love. (Psalm 147:9-11) (TLH, p. 118#7)

Lord God, heavenly Father, we thank you for all your gifts, through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#8)

Prayer before receiving the sacrament

O God, you do not desire the death of sinners, but that they turn from their evil ways and live. I come to you, although I have sinned and deserve only your wrath. But I flee to your mercy in Christ Jesus, my Lord, who gave his body and his blood for my redemption. Lord, grant that I may always believe this and never waver. Grant that in faith I may worthily go to your altar to receive the true body and the true blood which your Son has given for my salvation, that I may duly praise, laud, and honor your love and your mercy all the days of my life. Hear me for the sake of Jesus Christ, your Son, my Redeemer and Savior. Amen.  (TLH, p. 118#9)

Prayer After receiving the sacrament

Thanks and praise to you, almighty, eternal God, heavenly Father, for this your divine tenderness and love that you have again given me grace to receive the holy body and the precious blood of your only Son, Jesus Christ, my Lord. I humbly pray, fill me with the power of your Holy Spirit that through this Sacrament which I have received with my mouth I by faith may hold the treasures of your grace given to me in this Sacrament, namely the forgiveness of sins, oneness with Christ, and eternal life. Let your grace enable me to walk steadfast in the footsteps of my Lord Jesus Christ, never doubting that at the last you wilt give me and all who bear the cross for his sake the crown of eternal life. Hear me, heavenly Father, for the sake of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Savior. Amen. (TLH, p. 118#10)

For the sick and the dying

O Lord Jesus, you have made it my lot to bear the cross. Give me an obedient and submissive heart that I may willingly take your yoke and follow you in every affliction. Amen. (TLH, p. 119#1)

Almighty God, you forgive all our iniquities and heal all our diseases. You have proclaimed your name to be ‘the Lord who heals us,’ and have sent your beloved son to bear our sicknesses. Look on your unworthy servants with mercy. Pardon and forgive our transgressions. In your lovingkindness, remove the sickness which you have allowed to come on us; we ask according to your will, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (TLH, p. 119#2)

O Christ, Son of God, you bore the pain of the cross for him and died for his sins. Have mercy on him, forgive his sins, and do not let his faith fail. Amen. (TLH, p. 119#3)

O God, the Holy Spirit, our true Comforter in all distress, uphold him in patience and prayer. Sanctify him with full assurance, and do not forsake him in his last hour. Take him from this world of sorrow to his heavenly home. Amen. (TLH, p. 119#4)

Almighty, eternal and most merciful God, you summon and take us out of this sinful and corrupt world to yourself through death so that we may not perish or continue in sin, but pass through death to life eternal. Help us to know and believe this with our whole heart that we may rejoice in our departure and at your call cheerfully enter your eternal kingdom; through Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord. Amen. (TLH, p. 119#5)

Depart in peace, ransomed soul, in the name of God the Father almighty who created you, in the name of Jesus + Christ, the Son of the living God, who redeemed you, in the name of the Holy Spirit, who sanctified you. Come now to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering, and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven. The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forevermore. (Psalm 121:8) Amen. (TLH, p. 119#6)

Numbers for TLH refer to the prayers on pp. 102-109 in The Lutheran Hymnal. The prayers in The Lutheran Hymnal seem to be from an earlier collection which Common Service Book expanded. Even though The Lutheran Hymnal was produced later (1941), they reprinted the earlier collection of the prayers.

title: General Prayers
subtitle: ELHB Section
text:
The Litany, Suffrages, and general prayers, together with the contemporary English revisions linked from the source page. Original text General Prayers

I.

The Litany

The Litany may be used at Evening Service on Sundays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, on Days of Humiliation and Prayer, and at Morning Service on Sundays when there is no Communion. The Responses may be repeated after each phrase, or only at the end of each group, as here followeth:

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

O Christ, hear us.

O Christ, hear us.

O God, the Father in heaven;

Have mercy upon us.

O God the Son, Redeemer of the world;

Have mercy upon us.

O God, the Holy Ghost;

Have mercy upon us.

<w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="360"/></w:tabs></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00B46795"><w:t xml:space="preserve">

Be gracious unto us.

Spare us, good Lord.

Be gracious unto us.

Help us, good Lord.

From all sin;

From all error;

From all evil:

Good Lord, deliver us.

From the crafts and assaults of the devil;

From sudden and evil death;

From pestilence and famine;

From war and bloodshed;

From sedition and rebellion;

From lightning and tempest;

From all calamity by fire and water;

And from everlasting death:

Good Lord, deliver us.

By the mystery of Thy holy Incarnation;

By Thy holy Nativity;

By Thy baptism, fasting, and temptation;

By Thine agony and bloody sweat;

By Thy cross and Passion;

By Thy precious death and burial;

By Thy glorious resurrection and ascension;

And by the coming of the Holy Ghost, the Comforter:

Help us, good Lord.

In all time of our tribulation;

In all time of our prosperity;

In the hour of death;

And in the day of judgment:

Help us, good Lord.

We poor sinners do beseech Thee;

To hear us, O Lord God.

And to rule and govern Thy holy Christian Church;

To preserve all pastors and ministers of Thy Church in the true knowledge and

understanding of Thy Word, and in holiness of life;

To put an end to all schisms and causes of offence;

To bring into the way of truth all such as have erred, and are deceived;

To beat down Satan under our feet;

To send faithful laborers into Thy harvest;

To accompany Thy Word with Thy Spirit and grace;

To raise up them that fall, and to strengthen such as do stand;

And to comfort and help the weak-hearted and the distressed:

We beseech Thee to hear us, good Lord.

To give to all nations peace and concord;

To preserve our country from discord and contention;

To give to our nation perpetual victory over all its enemies;

To direct and defend our President, and all in authority;

And to bless and keep our magistrates, and all our people:

We beseech Thee to hear us, good Lord.

To behold and succor all who are in danger, necessity, and tribulation;

To protect all who travel by land or water;

To preserve all women in the perils of childbirth;

To strengthen and keep all sick persons and young children;

To set free all who are innocently imprisoned;

To defend and provide for all fatherless children and widows;

And to have mercy upon all men:

We beseech Thee to hear us, good Lord.

To forgive our enemies, persecutors, and slanderers, and to turn their hearts;

To give and preserve to our use the fruits of the earth;

And graciously to hear our prayers:

We beseech Thee to hear us, good Lord.

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God;

We beseech Thee to hear us.

O Lamb of God, that takest away the sin of the world;

Have mercy upon us.

O Lamb of God, that takest away the sin of the world;

Have mercy upon us.

O Lamb of God, that takest away the sin of the world;

Grant us Thy peace.

O Christ, hear us.

O Christ, hear us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us. Amen.

Then shall the Minister, and the Congregation with him, say the Lord's Prayer, after which may be said one or more of the Litany Collects here following:

Our Father, who art in heaven; Hallowed be Thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven; Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; And lead us not into temptation; But deliver us from evil; For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever and ever. Amen.

LITANY COLLECTS.

1

M. O Lord, deal not with us after our sins.

C. Neither reward us according to our iniquities.

Almighty God, our heavenly Father, who desirest not the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn from his evil way and live: We beseech Thee graciously to turn from us those punishments which we by our sins have deserved, and to grant us grace ever hereafter to serve Thee in holiness and pureness of living; through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord. Amen.

2

M. Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Thy Name.

C. Deliver us, and purge away our sins, for Thy Name's sake.

Almighty and Everlasting God, who by Thy Holy Spirit dost govern and sanctify the whole Christian Church, hear our prayers for all members of the same, and mercifully grant, that by Thy grace they may serve Thee in true faith; through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord.  Amen.

3

M. O Lord, deal not with us after our sins.

C. Neither reward us according to our iniquities.

O God, merciful Father, who despisest not the sighing of a contrite heart, nor the desire of such as are sorrowful: Mercifully assist our prayers which we make before Thee in all our troubles and adversities whensoever they oppress us; and graciously hear us that those evils which the craft and subtilty of the devil or man worketh against us, may, by Thy good providence, be brought to naught; that we

<w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="360"/></w:tabs></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00B46795"><w:t>Thy servants, being hurt by no persecutions, may evermore give thanks unto Thee in Thy holy Church; through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord. Amen.

4

M. O Lord, enter not into judgment with Thy servant.

C. For in Thy sight shall no man living be justified.

Almighty God, who knowest us to be set in the midst of so many and great dangers, that by reason of the frailty of our nature we cannot always stand upright: Grant us such strength and protection, as may support us in all dangers, and carry us through all temptations; through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord. Amen.

5

M. Call upon Me in the day of trouble.

C. I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me.

Spare us, O Lord, and mercifully forgive us our sins, and though by our continual transgressions we have merited Thy punishments, be gracious unto us, and grant that all those evils which we have deserved, may be turned from us, and overruled to our everlasting good; through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord. Amen.

6

FOR PEACE

M. The Lord will give strength unto His people.

C. The Lord will bless His people with peace.

O God, from whom all holy desires, all good counsels, and all just works do proceed: Give unto Thy servants that peace, which the world cannot give; that our hearts may be set to obey Thy commandments, and also that by Thee, we, being defended from the fear of our enemies, may pass our time in rest and quietness; through the merits of Jesus Christ our Savior. Amen.

II.

The Suffrages.

The Suffrages may be used at Early or Evening Service in the same manner as the Litany.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Our Father, who art in heaven; Hallowed be Thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven; Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; And lead us not into temptation.

But deliver us from evil.

I said; O Lord, be merciful unto me;

Heal my soul; for I have sinned against Thee.

Return, O Lord, how long?

And let it repent Thee concerning Thy servants.

Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us;

According as we hope in Thee.

Let Thy priests be clothed with righteousness;

And let Thy saints shout for joy.

O Lord, save our rulers;

Let the King hear us when we call.

Save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance;

Feed them also, and lift them up for ever.

Remember Thy congregation;

Which Thou hast purchased of old.

Peace be within thy walls;

And prosperity within thy palaces.

Let us pray for our absent brethren;

O Thou, our God, save Thy servants that trust in Thee.

Let us pray for the broken-hearted and the captives;

Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

Send them help from the Sanctuary.

And strengthen them out of Zion.

Hear my prayer, O LORD;

And let my cry come unto Thee.

Then may be said responsively, by the Minister and Congregation, the Psalm De Profundis (130) at Early Morning Service, and at Evening Service, Psalm Miserere Mei (51).

Ps. CXXX. De Profundis.

Out of the depths have I cried:

Unto Thee O Lord.

Lord, hear my voice:

Let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.

If Thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities:

Lord, who shall stand?

But there is forgiveness with Thee:

That Thou mayest be feared.

I wait for the Lord, my soul doth wait:

And in His Word do I hope.

My soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning:

I say, more than they that watch for the morning.

Let Israel hope in the Lord:

For with the Lord there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

And He shall redeem Israel:

From all his iniquities.

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost:

As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be world without end. Amen.

Or at Evening Service.

Ps. LI. Miserere mei.

Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy loving kindness:

According unto the multitude of Thy tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.

Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity:

And cleanse me from my sin.

For I acknowledge my transgressions:

And my sin is ever before me.

Against Thee, Thee only, have I sinned and done this evil in Thy sight;

That Thou mightest be justified when Thou speakest and be clear when Thou judgest.

Behold, I was shapen in iniquity:

And in sin did my mother conceive me.

Behold, Thou desirest truth in the inward parts:

And in the hidden part shalt Thou make me to know wisdom.

Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean:

Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

Make me to hear joy and gladness:

That the bones which Thou hast broken may rejoice.

Hide Thy face from my sins:

And blot out all mine iniquities.

Create in me a clean heart, O God:

And renew a right spirit within me.

Cast me not away from Thy presence:

And take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation:

And uphold me with Thy free Spirit.

Then will I teach transgressors Thy ways:

And sinners shall be converted unto Thee.

Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, Thou God of my salvation

And my tongue shall sing aloud of Tliy righteousness.

O Lord, open Thou my lips

And my mouth shall show forth Thy praise.

For Thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it:

Thou delightest not in burnt offering.

The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit:

A broken and a contrite heart, God, Thou wilt not despise.

Do good in Thy good pleasure unto Zion:

Build Thou the walls of Jerusalem.

Then shalt Thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt-offering and whole burnt

Offering:

Then shall they offer bullocks upon Thine altar.

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost:

As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Then shall be said:

Turn us again, O God of hosts;

Cause Thy face to shine and we shall be saved.

Arise, O Christ, for our help;

And redeem us, for Thy mercy’s sake.

Hear my prayer, O LORD;

And let my cry come unto Thee.

The Lord be with you.

And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.

Then shall the Minister say a Collect for the Season and any other suitable Collects, and after that he may say this Collect for peace.

Give peace in our days, O Lord:

Because there is none other that fighteth for us, except Thou, our God.

O Lord, let there be peace in Thy strength:

And abundance in Thy towers.

Let us pray.

O God, from whom all holy desires, all good counsels, and all just works do proceed: Give unto Thy servants that peace, which the world cannot give; that our hearts may be set to obey Thy commandments, and also that by Thee, we, being defended from the fear of our enemies, may pass our time in rest and quietness; through the merits of Jesus Christ our Savior.  Amen.

Then may be sung or said  the Benedicamus

Bless we the Lord:

Thanks be to God.

III.

The Morning Suffrages.

To be said at Early Morning Service, or in the Morning Prayer of the Household.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Christ, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Lord, have mercy upon us.

Then shall all say the Lord’s Prayer and the Apostles’ Creed:

Our Father, who art in heaven; Hallowed be Thy Name Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven; Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us; And lead us not into temptation; But deliver us from evil; For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth.

And in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord; Who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, Born of the Virgin Mary; Suffered under Pontius Pilate, Was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell; The third day He rose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, And sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; From thence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Ghost; The holy Christian Church, the Communion of Saints; The Forgiveness of sins; The Resurrection of the body; And the life everlasting. Amen.

Unto Thee have I cried, O LORD:

And in the morning shall my prayer prevent Thee.

Let my mouth be filled with Thy praise:

And with Thy honor all the day.

O Lord, hide Thy face from my sins:

And blot out all mine iniquities.

Create in me a clean hear, O God:

And renew a right spirit within me.

Cast me not away from Thy presence:

And take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation:

And uphold me with Thy free Spirit.

Vouchsafe, O Lord, this day:

To keep us without sin.

Have mercy upon us, O Lord:

Have mercy upon us.

O Lord, let Thy mercy be upon us:

As our trust is in Thee.

Hear my prayer, O LORD:

And let my cry come unto Thee.

The Lord be with you.

And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.

Then shall be said the prayer here following, or No 46 or No. 60, of the Collects and Prayers, or any suitable prayer.

We give thanks unto Thee, heavenly Father, through Jesus Christ Thy dear Son, that Thou hast protected us through the night from all danger and harm; and we beseech Thee to pereserve and keep us this day also from all sin and evil, that in all our thoughts, words, and deeds we may serve and please Thee. Into Thy hands we commend our bodies and souls and all that is ours. Let Thy holy angel have charge concerning us that the Wicked One have no power over us. Amen.

<w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="450"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="916"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="1832"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="2748"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="3664"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="4580"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="5496"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="6412"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="7328"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="8244"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="9160"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="10076"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="10992"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="11908"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="12824"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="13740"/><w:tab w:val="left" w:pos="14656"/></w:tabs><w:jc w:val="center"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:eastAsia="Times New Roman"/><w:i/><w:color w:val="FF0000"/><w:sz w:val="24"/><w:szCs w:val="24"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:proofErr w:type="spellStart"/><w:r w:rsidRPr="00DF3F54"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:eastAsia="Times New Roman"/><w:i/><w:color w:val="FF0000"/><w:sz w:val="24"/><w:szCs w:val="24"/></w:rPr><w:t>Benedicamus

Bless we the Lord:

Thanks be to God.
